newsitem.title: USA: Sen Moynihan delays effective date of stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Sen Moynihan delays effective date of stadium bill.

text.p: U.S. Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan reintroduced his controversial stadium financing bill with new language that delays the measure's effective date, his office said on Thursday.

The new version would take effect on the day it is signed by the President, rather on the day that a U.S. House or Senate committee votes on the measure, in a move designed to calm market concerns about upcoming stadium bond deals, an aide to Moynihan, D-N.Y., said.
Moynihan's bill, originally introduced in 1996, would bar use of tax-exempt government bonds to finance construction of professional sports stadiums.
The original bill had a June 14, 1995, effective date, which drew a chorus of criticism from bond groups that said the retroactive date was chilling the market for stadium bonds.
Moynihan reoffered the bill in late January 1996, delaying the effective date to the day that a congressional committee votes on the measure.

Moynihan recently signaled that he would delay the effective date even further when Sen. Arlen Specter, R-Pa., threatened to block action on another bill shepherded by Moynihan involving aviation taxes if the stadiums effective date was not pushed back.
Late on March 12, Moynihan inserted a statement in the Congressional Record stating that he agrees to the Specter request.
